reason: The original Greek leaves for John 18:14–20:13 are lost. The gap was filled in later by another hand, so the text here is not the 5th-century copy.
The purple codex is scattered across several libraries; nothing survives between John 16:15 and 20:23.
A palimpsest; only John 1:29–40, 2:13–25 and 21:1–11 survive.
Greek text of John survives only as far as 8:31.
The majuscule hand stops at John 8:39; the rest was supplied in minuscule in the 13th century.
Starts at John 18:36, just after our verse.
All contain John 18 but fall after the AD 900 cut-off for this first version. (028 S is precisely dated to 949 by its scribe’s note.)
